reasoning_quality_informational.v1_root_problem: Dispute tickets have doubled since August 2026 (E-03) despite ticket response times staying within the 3.0-day SLA (E-01), ruling out response speed as the driver; manual meter-read route completion for 9200 accounts fell to 0.88 against a 0.95 target in Aug-Sep (E-05, attributed by SH-FIELD to a reader shortfall, E-07), forcing estimate-substitution billing reflected in the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-02). The larger 1785-bill ACTUAL-read-type majority of disputes (E-02) is not explained by this mechanism, and with no tariff changes logged (E-04, E-06), a separate billing-side mechanism remains unconfirmed.
reasoning_quality_informational.v2_root_problem: Billing import validation rule BV-17, deployed 2026-08-01, compares raw AMI register values against 12-month m3 history with unit_scaling set to none (E-13); because firmware v4.2 meters, rolled out 2026-06, register consumption in 0.1 m3 units instead of whole m3 (E-14), BV-17 misreads normal v4.2 consumption as abnormally high. This rejected 1184 arriving, exported v4.2 AMI reads as REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION at import (E-12), forcing estimate substitution behind a large share of the 1240 ESTIMATED-type disputed bills (E-02) and coinciding with the August dispute-volume doubling (E-03); the same unit-scaling defect can also miscompute accepted v4.2 ACTUAL-read bills, giving a billing-side mechanism for part of the larger 1785-bill ACTUAL-type dispute share (E-02, E-13, E-14).
reasoning_quality_informational.ideal_final_problem: BV-17 validation rejects valid firmware-v4.2 AMI reads (unit-scale mismatch on H-MDMS-BILL) and substitutes estimates.
